page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration belonging to the N1 family. It is built on an x86_64 Intel Xeon processor clocked at 2.3 GHz, supplying 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 45 MB of L3 cache, along with basic instruction set extensions including AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, though it lacks modern AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Memory capacity is substantial, offering 104.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 6.5 GB per vCPU. It includes zero bundled local storage and has no integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear separation between single-core throughput and multi-threaded system capacity. Single-core performance is limited, with Geekbench single-core at 937.0 and stress-ng single-core performance scoring 1113.69, both placing in the lowest tiers. Single-threaded gzip compression (18.85 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (7.15 GB/sec) reflect this architectural constraint. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics stabilize in the middle percentiles, recording a PassMark CPU score of 12812.02 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5935.0. Memory subsystems achieve 81.5 GB/sec read and 43.43 GB/sec write throughput for large uncached blocks, supporting 10.99 million Redis SET operations per second.

Resource allocation trades raw single-thread computational speed for large memory capacity per virtual core. With 104 GB of system RAM, it provides cost-effective memory density for applications constrained by data size rather than CPU execution speed. It is effectively deployed for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database nodes, ETL batch pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise enterprise workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon architecture operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance delivers 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with dedicated hyperthreading and provides 104.0 GB of RAM (6.5 GB per vCPU). It does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its single-core compute performance in the lower percentiles, but multi-threaded and memory throughput metrics rank squarely in the median ranges, evidenced by 10.99 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5935.0. Lacking AVX-512 extensions and bundled NVMe drives, this instance is primarily configured for memory-intensive enterprise tasks such as database hosting, large-scale in-memory caching, and memory-heavy batch processing.
